name: AZ-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+4 district with Democratic incumbent Greg Stanton running for reelection
Stanton's large financial advantage: $2.0M cash on hand vs. $342K for Jasser, with no outside opposition spending
Polymarket prices Stanton at 94% to win
No public general-election polling in the race
model.rationale: Stanton holds a D+4 seat with strong incumbency and a roughly four-to-one fundraising edge, while markets price him near certain and no outside groups are opposing him. With no contrary polling or ratings, the fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit win.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Stanton or a favorable Republican national environment could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat remains a long shot.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Greg Stanton seeks a fourth term in this Phoenix-area district that leans Democratic by about four points. He enters the general election with a substantial resource advantage, having raised over $2.1 million and holding roughly $2.0 million on hand, while Republican nominee Zuhdi Jasser has raised about $565,000 with $342,000 available. No outside groups have spent against the incumbent.

Prediction markets give Stanton roughly a 94 percent chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. There is no public general-election polling, so the outlook rests on fundamentals: the district lean, incumbency, and the money gap all favor Stanton. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
